IMF Asia chief Krishna Srinivasan on what could derail India's 7% growth outlookThe IMF has raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 7% from 6.4%, but warned that converging global risks could weigh on the outlook. He warned that the energy crisis could worsen, fuelling inflation and slowing growth, and called for energy diversification and greater efficiency. Srinivasan said the rupee should be allowed to adjust to external shocks, while monetary policy should respond if depreciation fuels inflation. He welcomed India's trade deals but stressed the need for reforms to attract investment. He also called for reskilling workers to adapt to AI and cautioned that El Nino could hurt agriculture and growth.
